title: Converge Learn-it Atlas on one learning journey
purpose: Implement the smallest post-Human-Replay correction justified by real Atlas use on R11: fail closed so only runtime-qualified content enters the Atlas journey, remove course-progress chrome from the active question surface, clarify the pre-session transition, make Library progress segments self-describing, quiet the rename affordance, simplify ambiguous progress glyphs, and stop offering pointless same-day repetition when every objective is already independently validated and waiting for its next memory interval. Memory, evidence, planner, scoring, storage, contracts and authoring content remain unchanged.
invariants: Atlas learning actions from Today and Library continue to enter the same existing Atlas planner/session engine.
Only a context accepted by the existing Atlas claim authority may be presented as an Atlas learning journey; unsupported kits remain handled outside that journey.
An active Atlas activity owns the learner surface: course-level progress and recommendation chrome must not remain above the question.

When all objectives are already independently validated and not yet due for reconfirmation, presentation may suppress an immediate session action but must not change recommendation, evidence, memory or planner semantics.
The 5/15/30 duration policy and frozen planner construction are unchanged whenever a session is available.
Canonical evidence states, transitions, scoring, projection, learning-event semantics, history and resume state are unchanged.
learnit.kit.v2, authoring payloads, claim authority, accepted claim set and import semantics are unchanged.
No synthetic progress percentage or new learner state is introduced.
requiredEvidence: PR #354 exact parent R11 head 934e1c7193fc6d20d408339f8a962bca6aea51a6 is recorded before mutation.
Static and regression evidence proves compatibleAtlasCourse requires claimAuthority.contextAccepted(context).
The previously used neutral qualification kit cannot masquerade as a fully qualified Atlas validation journey merely because it contains estimatedMinutes and claim-shaped fields.
The existing claim-authority-qualified Atlas content remains eligible for the Atlas surface.
While data-atlas-session-active=true, the enclosing course-row main/progress chrome is hidden and the active question surface remains focused.
Library objective segments expose the objective label and learner-facing state on hover through native title text.
Pre-session preview explicitly frames itself as the upcoming session rather than appearing as an unexplained intermediate mode.

When every ranked objective is validated-recently, its memory dueAt is in the future and the fallback recommendation would only repeat practice, Today and Library expose an 'À jour pour aujourd’hui' rest state with the next useful date instead of another immediate session control.
The atlas.memory-policy.v1 intervals remain exactly 1, 3, 7 and 21 days.
Ambiguous R9 status glyphs are no longer the primary visible encoding; textual learner states and existing state styling remain available without a synthetic percentage.
Existing Atlas core, learning, experience, integration and UX-clarity suites remain green.
The deterministic source manifest is rebound to all changed source/test files.
Exact-head PR CI passes before a new Human Replay is published.
adversarialTests: Do not broaden runtime claim authority or accept arbitrary authored claims in this UX patch.
Do not change atlas_memory.js intervals or manipulate time to make the replay reach acquisition faster.
Do not replace the rest-state presentation with a new evidence state or persisted flag.
Do not suppress active-session progress by hiding the question, feedback or answer controls.
Do not add a synthetic percentage or infer progress beyond existing evidence states.
Do not modify authoring kits, contracts, storage, scoring, projection or import semantics.
Do not create a new QA programme or declare learner usability PASS from machine evidence.
nonGoals: Changing learnit.kit.v2 or any EPF/authoring kit payload.
Expanding the frozen accepted Atlas claim set to the neutral Human Replay fixture.
Changing Atlas memory spacing, planner duration policy, recommendation semantics, evidence states or scoring.
Creating persistent chapter, group, phase, parent-child hierarchy or a new progress metric.
Adding manual objective selection, favorites, an override algorithm or a new learning mode.
Creating a new runtime, backend, dashboard or contradictory-QA chain.
independentReview: Human Replay R11/R12 evidence is treated as learner observation, not as an instruction to implement every suggestion.
The active-session screenshot directly contradicts issue #352 because course-level progress remains above the question; this is a product regression and is corrected.

The neutral qualification fixture exposed a test-instrumentation defect: surface compatibility accepted content that the frozen runtime claim authority could never validate. Fail-closed admission is smaller and safer than expanding claim authority under #352.

The observed same-day loop has two causes: the neutral fixture could not produce admissible validation, and validated-recently legitimately uses spaced memory intervals. The patch fixes the misleading surface behavior without changing the 1/3/7/21 policy.
The user's inline-title rename idea is not adopted; the existing disclosure is simply made quieter and shorter.
The user's request for progress clarity is addressed by reducing ambiguous glyph prominence and retaining explicit state labels, not by inventing a percentage.
No learner usability PASS is owned by this implementation stream.
rollback: Revert the bounded R12 commits or reset PR #354 to exact R11 head 934e1c7193fc6d20d408339f8a962bca6aea51a6. No persisted state, contract, kit, claim-authority or memory-policy schema is changed.
